notes.note: Every price, per-unit figure and cap rate in this set is illustrative. The per-unit price is a round number chosen to sit inside the band a real per-unit sale price occupies, so the cap-rate arithmetic is realistic. It is not a quote, an offer, a broker's guidance, or a valuation. Cap rates move inversely with the price, so read them as a demonstration of the mechanics rather than a view on the asset.

notes.topic: Licensed data is excluded by design, not by omission
notes.note: No subscription or licensed market-data feed appears anywhere in this set. Comps come only from an operator's own weekly scrape of public leasing pages. That is a deliberate constraint, not a gap: licensed data cannot travel outside the licence, so a portfolio piece built on it could not be shown at all. The cost is coverage, and the coverage is measured and stated rather than assumed.

notes.topic: Comp radius is stated, and coverage inside it is measured
notes.note: The comp block states the radius it searched and how many tracked communities inside it carry live rents; that sentence is counted from the operator's own scrape, never written by hand. The detail tiers are the closest same-product communities within that radius, so a wide radius adds nearby candidates without letting a distant one outrank a close one. A community the scrape tracks but could not quote is listed nearby with the reason rather than dropped.

The detailed tiers hold only communities within ten years of the subject's year built. Widening that range changes which communities are in the set, and a set that includes materially newer product will generally report a different rent — how much, and in which direction, is a property of the particular submarket and date, not a rule. Where this output set has measured the difference between two otherwise-identical comp sets on its own subject, the figures appear in the note below.

notes.topic: Year built comes from a free-text note, where it exists at all
notes.note: The rent tracker has no year-built column. Where a vintage appears here it was parsed out of a free-text note on the community record, and every row carries that as its source. A community with no such note keeps its place in the comp set on distance and product, shows a dash for the year, and the tier header says how many rows the vintage filter could not be applied to. Inventing a year would fabricate the evidence the filter runs on; dropping the community would hide the closest comps for want of a field the source never had.

notes.topic: Market rent is never a blend of new and renewal
notes.note: Market rent for the model is the new-lease average where a plan has new leases inside the lookback window, and in-place rent where it does not. It is never the average of new and renewal leases together. A blended figure reads as market rent and is not one: renewals are priced off the existing rent, so blending them in drags the number toward where rents used to be and understates the gap the underwriting is trying to measure. On an asset whose in-place rents sit above what the market is currently signing, the rule produces a market rent BELOW in-place — which is the correct and uncomfortable answer, and the one a blend would hide.

notes.topic: Estimated values are not published as facts
notes.note: Where a figure is derived rather than read, the audit trail says so and names the inputs. Where a figure is unknown, the cell shows a visible hole rather than a plausible-looking number. A blank that reads as a zero is the most expensive kind of missing data, because nothing downstream flags it.

notes.topic: What the public demo leaves to the internal pipeline
notes.note: This demo is a deliberately reduced copy of the operator's pipeline. A licensed data source, a county-portal login, a school-rating lookup, a web valuation or a lease trade-out report is not something a public page should reach or ask for, so the values those produce — the assessor's parcel and bill, school ratings, a fair market value, the new-versus-renewal trade-out — read 'Internal pipeline only' with the reason wherever they appear. The field manifest lists every one of them. Everything else on these tabs is produced the same way for the sample and for an uploaded deal, from the same sources.

notes.topic: Supply coverage is an area of ongoing work
notes.note: The supply section is real and unmodified — the rings, stages and unit counts come from a public permit and entitlement pipeline, and a zero is a genuine zero rather than a gap left blank. Coverage of that pipeline is an area of ongoing work: a ring showing no active supply means nothing was matched in the sources covered so far, which is a weaker statement than nothing being built. This section will be expanded; read it as a floor on competing supply, not a census of it.

notes.topic: Checks degrade to NOT CHECKED rather than passing quietly
notes.note: Every cross-tie on the checks tab reports OK, FAIL, or NOT CHECKED. A check missing one of its inputs reports NOT CHECKED and claims no difference — it never reports OK. A green result that only means 'this check could not run' is worse than a red one, because it buys confidence it has not earned.

notes.topic: What vintage-matching changed on this deal
notes.note: This subject was built 1981. Two comp sets were selected by identical criteria — same candidate pool, same product test, same tracker exclusions, same radius, same closest-20 cap, same rent rules, same mix weighting — differing only in whether the +/-10-year vintage test was applied. Set A, vintage test ON: 10 communities, vintages 1981 to 1987; this subject's rent reads 12.1% above it. Set B, vintage test OFF: 3 more communities join and none drops out — fewer than 20 qualify either way, so the cap never binds (vintages 1981 to 2018); the same rent reads 8.0% above it. Both figures are weighted by this property's own unit mix and computed over the same bed counts (95% of its units), so the two sets differ by 4.1 points. Every community that joins was built after 1987, set A's newest, so set B reaches newer product than the vintage test allowed. Both sets are listed on the Rent Comps section — this is a measurement of these two sets on this date, not an estimate of what vintage is worth in this market.

notes.topic: Market rent is BELOW in-place on this deal
notes.note: Unit-weighted in-place rent is $1,457 and market rent for the model is $1,345 — -7.7%. That is not an error. New leases are signing below what residents in place are paying, so the no-blend rule surfaces a downward mark the model has to carry. A blended new-and-renewal average would have hidden it.

IX sec. 18; A.R.S. sec. 42-13301) the LPV rises at most 5% a year and does not reset on sale, so a buyer inherits the seller's basis and tax priced off the purchase price overstates the bill — roughly threefold on the showcase parcel. demand.ring_1mi_caveat: The 1-mile column overstates levels. Ring membership is decided by each census block group's internal point, then the whole block group is counted — at 1 mile a single large block group can sit mostly outside the ring and still be counted whole. Measured against a commercial source, 1-mile population reads roughly 2.3x and households roughly 1.9x too high. The 3-, 5- and 10-mile columns do not have this problem. Read the 1-mile column for MIX and SHARES (income distribution, renter share, sector concentration), which are ratios and survive the overcount, and read levels off the 3-mile column.

transfer_tax.caveat: The constitution bars any NEW transfer tax imposed after 2007-12-31; it does not repeal pre-existing ones, and Arizona had none ad valorem. A flat $2 deed fee (A.R.S. 11-1132(A)) and a $30-per-instrument recording fee (A.R.S. 11-475(A)(1)) still apply and are not percentage-based.

mortgage_tax.rate_label: No mortgage or recording tax on the security instrument
mortgage_tax.citation: Ariz. Const. art. IX, sec. 24; A.R.S. 11-475(A)(1)
mortgage_tax.caveat: Recording is a flat per-instrument fee, not a tax on the amount borrowed.

closing_costs.note: Transfer tax is computed on the purchase price. A mortgage or recording tax is computed on the LOAN AMOUNT, and is reported as not asserted when no loan is stated — never inferred from the price, which would assume 100% leverage. Rates are verified against a primary authority and carry the citation and the date confirmed; a state absent from the table reports as not asserted rather than as zero.
